title: The decision interval holds the model's fit-to-fit spread (dclab-core 0.120.0)
request: The owner, 2026-10-26: build the next step for the daily range (add the model's fit-to-fit spread to the samples), tested, reviewed, and measured as time_decision_v5 with the gate fixed before; keep the machine light.
spec: dclab_core.decide.choose_operating_point(sample_scores=): K refit score vectors; each holdout-sized sample ranks its rows by one refit drawn at random. Engine _refit_scores: 10 refits of the selected model (rn.fit_and_predict) on bootstrap resamples of the latest fold's training rows (whole entities when a group column is set), scoring the latest fold's out-of-fold rows; skipped with a note when ten fits would take over 120 s or a refit fails. time_decision_v5: 60 fresh seeds, the daily arm, the drift off, v1's gate; each run keeps v4's interval (no refits) and the every-fold one, whether refits were used, and each refit's latest-fold AUC beside the fold model's.
plan: Map how the engine fits fold and final models
Failing core tests: refits widen on average, equal refits change nothing, refusals
Engine: refit on resamples of the latest fold's training rows

decisions.decision: Refits on bootstrap resamples of the latest fold's training rows, scoring the latest fold's rows
decisions.why: the samples come from the latest fold; a refit never scores a row it was fitted on, and the holdout's ranking is by a model fitted once more

decisions.decision: 10 refits, skipped with a note when ten of the fold's fits would take over 120 s
decisions.why: the owner: keep the machine light; the cost stays bounded on a large table

decisions.decision: The core test reads the widening as an average over three tables
decisions.why: measured on five synthetic tables: four wider by 10 to 25%, one narrower; widening is not a promise for one table

decisions.decision: The refits are off by default (engine.REFITS = 0); the core option and the engine code stay, on with REFITS = 10
decisions.why: the owner, 2026-10-26, on time_decision_v5's paired reading: the refits widen the daily interval by 1% for about 20 s a decision, and the same seeds passed without them

change: dclab_core/decide.py (sample_scores); dclab_rnd/studio/engine.py (_refit_scores, REFITS, REFIT_SECONDS); dclab_rnd/time_decision_measure.py (v5); tests/test_core_decide_holdout_interval.py (2 tests), tests/test_time_decision_measure.py (a failed-refit test and v5's readings); dclab_core 0.120.0, CHANGELOG, CORE_INTEGRATION.md, the plan

findings.defect: the first widening test made refits worse rankers than the model
findings.scenario: refits were the true probabilities plus noise, the model the true probabilities: every refit ranked worse, the interval moved down and came out narrower (3.21 against 3.41)
findings.cause: the test's refits were not as good as the model they stand for
findings.fix: the model and each refit carry the same noise around the truth: as good, ranking otherwise

findings.defect: the campaign's paired reading passed refit scores without their rows
findings.scenario: the every-fold paired call set sample_rows to None but kept sample_scores; the core refused it and the engine reported 'decision could not be computed'
findings.cause: a new argument not cleared in the paired call
findings.fix: the paired calls clear sample_scores too (and v5 keeps a no-refits reading)

findings.defect: the gate's 'paired' key was written twice
findings.scenario: the second copy (the old text) won, so the manifest never recorded the no-refits pairing
findings.cause: a dict literal edited by insertion
findings.fix: one key; refits_used named in the gate

findings.defect: a seed whose refits failed would be gated as a refit seed
findings.scenario: _refit_scores caught every error and returned None; the run passed 'chosen' and its z (v4's method) entered v5's width gate
findings.cause: the gate read the warning, not the method
findings.fix: each run records refits_used; the gate reads refit seeds only and names the rest; the note says why (the error's name, or the cost)

findings.defect: the pooled reading mixed two methods
findings.scenario: v4's z without refits pooled with v5's z with refits measures neither
findings.cause: pooling by arm, not by method
findings.fix: v4's readings pooled with v5's paired no-refits readings; v5's refit seeds read apart

findings.defect: the next step for a still-narrow interval would have been a leak
findings.scenario: refitting on every training row would score latest-fold rows the refits were fitted on: a falsely narrow spread and a high centre (CLAUDE.md rule 2)
findings.cause: a remedy written without asking which rows the refits score
findings.fix: out-of-bag refits on every fold's rows: each row scored only by refits whose resample left it out

findings.defect: rows of one entity were resampled apart
findings.scenario: on time_group data a row bootstrap draws one entity's rows independently, understating the fit-to-fit spread
findings.fix: whole entities resampled when the solution has a group column

findings.defect: v5 could pass from weaker refits
findings.scenario: a bootstrap resample holds about 63% of the rows, so a refit is weaker than the final model: a lower tail and centre could look like a right width
findings.fix: each run keeps each refit's latest-fold AUC beside the fold model's, and the no-refits interval's centre

measurements.name: time_decision_v5: the refits' spread (dclab-core 0.120.0), 60 fresh seeds (250 to 309), one call a day, the drift off, on f2f5394d
measurements.result: pass: 52 of 60 inside (5 below, 3 above), mean z -0.05 (bound 0.21), RMS z 1.11 (0.97 to 1.31); no seed left out without refits. Paired on the same seeds: without refits RMS z 1.12, 51 inside, mean z -0.10; from every fold RMS z 1.06, 52 inside. The refit interval is 1.012 times as wide, its centre -0.079 lower. Refit AUC 0.728 against the fold model's 0.732. v4's and v5's seeds without refits (120): 103 inside, RMS z 1.16; RMS z 1.16 means the misses run about 15% wider than the interval says
limits: the pass is not the refits' doing: the same seeds pass without them
pooled without refits the daily interval stays about 15% narrow, cause not found

outcome: The gate passed, but the paired reading shows the refits barely move the interval (1% wider); the pass is the seeds'. The daily interval stays about 15% narrow over 120 seeds, with drift, the pool and the fit-to-fit spread ruled out. The refits are off by default, the owner's call; the code stays.
lessons: A remedy for an interval must never let a model score rows it was fitted on: check which rows each refit sees
When a fix can widen an interval for a wrong reason (weaker refits), record what tells the reasons apart before the run
A pass is not a cause: the paired reading on the same seeds showed the old method would have passed too
risks: Refits on 63% of the rows are weaker than the final model; the AUCs recorded say by how much
